description: SCITEX is a multidisciplinary team focused on Data Science, Statistics, Machine Learning, AI, and NASA Earth observation data. We aim to build a rigorous, data-driven solution with real-world impact using spatiotemporal analysis, forecasting, and anomaly detection. We welcome members with skills in GIS, remote sensing, environmental science, software development, data engineering, UX/UI, or scientific storytelling.
summary: NASA data make it easy to say an aquifer is draining. Oasis Paradox asks the next question: is that trend real? It is a web platform that tests trends in monthly NASA records (GRACE/GRACE-FO, GLDAS-2.2, GPM IMERG, MODIS and MERRA-2, 2004-2024) for seven irrigated aquifer regions, from California's Central Valley to Northwest India, with Ica, Peru, as our home case. Every case passes three checks: source (is the witness independent? GLDAS-2.2 assimilates GRACE), scale (does the GRACE footprint match the aquifer? Ica is about 3% of one footprint) and method (monthly series have memory). In a Monte Carlo simulation with no true trend and autocorrelation phi = 0.9, the classic Mann-Kendall test raises a false alarm in 63% of series; our rule, which requires a block bootstrap and an AR(1) regression to agree, in 5%. GRACE shows a loss in five regions (confirmed in four, likely in one), a confirmed rise over Ica and no proven change over the Guarani aquifer. Users pick an aquifer on a 3D globe, choose any period of 10 years or more, read each verdict with plain definitions, ask the Datron AI assistant about a result and download a ZIP to reproduce it.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Oasis Paradox is a trend detective for the world's irrigated aquifers. A user picks an aquifer on a 3D globe (seven regions: Central Valley, High Plains, Northwest India, the Arabian Saq aquifer, the Tigris-Euphrates basin, the Guarani aquifer and Ica-Villacuri in Peru) and gets, for each NASA variable, the rate of change per decade with a 95% confidence interval, a significance test that is robust to autocorrelation and a verdict: Confirmed trend, Likely trend, No proven change or Insufficient data. "No proven change" never means "no change".

HOW IT WORKS

1. Data: monthly series 2004-2024 extracted from NASA products through Google Earth Engine (GRACE/GRACE-FO JPL mascons, GLDAS-2.2, GPM IMERG V07, MODIS NDVI, evapotranspiration and land surface temperature over a cropland mask, MERRA-2 air temperature). Three series were cross-checked against NASA AppEEARS and the GES DISC archive (r >= 0.9998).

2. Statistics (Python): monthly anomalies, Sen's slope, classic Mann-Kendall as a reference, moving-block bootstrap (L = 36 months, B = 999) and regression with ARMA errors. A trend is confirmed only when both robust tests agree (p < 0.05). Every function is tested with synthetic series of known slope.

3. Three checks: source (GLDAS-2.2 is labeled "model fed by GRACE", not an independent witness), scale (the GRACE footprint against the aquifer area) and method (the "Test the tests" lab shows, with 100 animated Monte Carlo trials, how memory turns noise into false trends).

4. App (React, Vite, TypeScript) reads precomputed JSON results; the "Ask Datron" chat (Google Gemini) answers questions about the screen, quoting only the case-file numbers.

BENEFITS

It stops a common mistake before it is published: calling a trend real because a classic test said p < 0.05 on autocorrelated data. Students, teachers and researchers get the slope, the uncertainty, the reason for each verdict and a reproducible ZIP.

INTENDED IMPACT

Anyone about to write "NASA data show..." can check it first. In Ica, Peru, the tool shows why GRACE cannot see a local aquifer decline that the wells record (69% of monitored wells fall), and why the answer needs regular well data, not a stronger claim.

CREATIVITY

Instead of another trend map, the platform puts the tests themselves on trial and makes the verdict rule visible and reproducible.

FACTORS CONSIDERED AND LIMITATIONS

Study areas are approximate boxes and masks, not official aquifer boundaries. Extraction was cross-checked on three series. Ica wells have two readings each. MODIS Terra orbit drift affects surface temperature after about 2020. GRACE ends in 2024 in our pipeline.

NEXT STEPS

Regular well series (ANA or JUASVI), a pilot with researchers, any user-drawn region, extension to 2025 with PO.DAAC and automatic monthly updates.

For historical context, our GRACE estimate for Northwest India (18.5 km3 per year, 2004-2024) is close to the 17.7 +/- 4.5 km3 per year reported by Rodell et al. (2009) for 2002-2008 over a different study area.
